verdict: Qualified local cooperative-admission success; incomplete creation/adoption journal and no unrestricted deployment guarantee.
rejected_counterexamples: duplicate physical identity, ownership overwrite and conflicting alias rebinding
new operational dependency or queued operational publication after withdrawal
cleanup prerequisite disposal before successful target absence acknowledgement
mutated bytes or replacement inode at recorded sandbox path
candidate_policy: One durable global fence blocks all admission writes. Historical provenance survives withdrawal; newly acquired operational commit references fail. Adoption keeps eventual cleanup prerequisites pinned.
integration: Journal(db_path, sandbox_path, runtime_root=own_workstream_runtime) permits later integration in an explicitly scoped fresh sandbox. snapshot -> reserve -> verify -> begin_effect -> effect -> ack. Gate must independently bind saved-plan bytes and backend/configuration receipts.
limitations: Creation is not write-ahead protected: real exit leaves an unregistered orphan, retained without auto-deletion.
Adoption is a trusted caller assertion, not an actual provider import.
Complete registered membership/dependencies and cooperative publishers/deployments are assumed.
Global fencing sacrifices availability; identity mismatch leaves a blocked ticket with no cancellation API.
External mutation between check and unlink, direct database writes, distributed operation and power-loss durability are not established.
Commit association sets approximate DML graphs; no immutable chronology/evidence DAG, exactly-once or legal erasure claim.
next_experiment: Add creation WAL intent, then integrate a cooperative saved-plan gate and import-capable synthetic-file provider with independently validated physical receipts.
